language.script_notes: English dominant; French appears via federal bilingual signage.
false_friends: Pacific Northwest US (Washington/Oregon — nearly identical coastal conifer forest and mountains)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: As national; common on winding mountain/coastal highways.
road_furniture.curb_style: As national; dense formal infrastructure in Vancouver/Victoria.

architecture.roof_style: Steeper roofs common given heavy coastal rainfall; low-pitch roofs on mid-century Vancouver-area suburban stock.
architecture.roof_material: Asphalt shingle and metal roofing widespread.
architecture.wall_construction: Wood-frame construction as national default, often with a distinctly West Coast modern architectural style (large windows, natural wood, integration with forested/mountain surroundings) in and around Vancouver.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Natural wood tones and muted greens/greys against a dense evergreen backdrop.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Vancouver's modern glass-tower skyline set dramatically against the Coast Mountains and ocean; ferry terminals connecting Vancouver Island and the mainland; forestry industry infrastructure inland.

nature.vegetation: Dense temperate rainforest — Douglas fir, western hemlock, red cedar — covers much of the coast and mountains; drier grassland and ponderosa pine in the BC interior (Okanagan); alpine terrain at higher elevations.
nature.terrain: Rugged and mountainous throughout — the Coast Mountains and Insular Mountains (Vancouver Island, Haida Gwaii) dominate, with a deeply fjord-and-island-incised Pacific coastline (over 40,000 islands) and the Rocky Mountains along the eastern border with Alberta.
nature.climate_signature: Mild, wet, and green on the coast (Vancouver/Victoria); drier and more continental in the interior; consistently mountainous, dramatic scenery throughout.

vehicles.plate_color: Blue-on-white with a screened provincial flag — a distinctive and reliable BC-specific plate design.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: As national; higher EV/hybrid presence than the Prairies given BC's environmental policy and urban Vancouver population.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Dense, current coverage around Vancouver and Victoria.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very good coverage in populated coastal areas; real gaps in the mountainous, less-populated interior and northern BC.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Nearly identical Pacific coastal conifer forest (Douglas fir, cedar, hemlock), similar mountainous terrain and grey drizzly climate
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Canadian speed signage is in km/h (vs. US mph); BC's blue-on-white plate with the screened provincial flag differs from Washington's/Oregon's US state plates; French appears on some federally-mandated Canadian packaging/signage that wouldn't appear in the US.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Western Canada is mountainous coastal terrain; the East is forested/lake-covered lowland, the Prairies are flat farmland, and the North is Arctic tundra — all visually distinct.
